buildNotes: Every seesaw access is a write of two bytes, module base then function register; for a read wait about 8 ms, then read the bytes back, big-endian.

Buttons 1-4 are seesaw pins 18, 19, 20, 2: set them input with pull-up (DIRCLR_BULK 0x01 0x03, PULLENSET 0x01 0x0B, BULK_SET 0x01 0x05, mask 0x001C0004), then read GPIO_BULK (0x01 0x04, 4 bytes); a bit reads 0 while its button is pressed.
LEDs 1-4 are seesaw pins 12, 13, 0, 1: write 0x08 0x01 then pin, duty high byte, duty low byte (0-65535).
Default address 0x3A; cut A0/A1/A2/A3 on the back to add 1/2/4/8 (up to 0x49).
Arcade buttons and JST XH quick-connect cables are not included: plug each button's switch into SWITCHn and its LED into LEDn.
The two 6-pad rows carry the same signals; solder headers to both for a breadboard, or use a STEMMA QT / Qwiic cable.

driver.code:
# Adafruit LED Arcade Button 1x4 STEMMA QT I2C breakout (product 5296, ATtiny817 running seesaw firmware),
# MicroPython driver.
# seesaw protocol: every access starts with a write of [module base, function register];
# for a read, wait briefly, then read the bytes back (all values big-endian).
import time

_STATUS_BASE = 0x00
_STATUS_HW_ID = 0x01
_STATUS_SWRST = 0x7F
_GPIO_BASE = 0x01
_GPIO_DIRCLR_BULK = 0x03
_GPIO_BULK = 0x04
_GPIO_BULK_SET = 0x05
_GPIO_INTENSET = 0x08
_GPIO_INTENCLR = 0x09
_GPIO_PULLENSET = 0x0B
_TIMER_BASE = 0x08
_TIMER_PWM = 0x01

_HW_IDS = (0x87, 0x85, 0x89)  # ATtiny817 (this board); ATtiny807/1617 seesaw builds use the same pin map
BUTTON_PINS = (18, 19, 20, 2)  # SWITCH1, SW #2, SW #3, SWITCH4 (pressed = shorted to GND)
LED_PINS = (12, 13, 0, 1)      # LED1-LED4, PWM into BSS138 low-side switches from the on-board 5 V pump
_BUTTON_MASK = 0
for _p in BUTTON_PINS:
    _BUTTON_MASK |= 1 << _p


class ArcadeQT:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x3A, reset=True, interrupt=False):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if reset:
            self._write(_STATUS_BASE, _STATUS_SWRST, b'\xff')
            time.sleep_ms(500)  # seesaw restarts after a software reset
        hw = self._read(_STATUS_BASE, _STATUS_HW_ID, 1)[0]
        if hw not in _HW_IDS:
            raise OSError('seesaw not found at 0x%02x (HW_ID 0x%02x): check the wiring' % (addr, hw))
        # Buttons: inputs with pull-ups (a pressed button shorts the pin to GND).
        mask = _BUTTON_MASK.to_bytes(4, 'big')
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_DIRCLR_BULK, mask)
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_PULLENSET, mask)
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_BULK_SET, mask)
        self._write(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_INTENSET if interrupt else _GPIO_INTENCLR, mask)
        for i in range(4):
            self.led(i, 0)

    def _write(self, base, reg, data=b''):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([base, reg]) + bytes(data))

    def _read(self, base, reg, n, delay_us=8000):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([base, reg]))
        time.sleep_us(delay_us)  # seesaw needs time to fetch the value before the read
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, n)

    def buttons(self):
        """List of 4 booleans, True while button 1, 2, 3, 4 is pressed."""
        b = self._read(_GPIO_BASE, _GPIO_BULK, 4)
        bits = (b[0] << 24) | (b[1] << 16) | (b[2] << 8) | b[3]
        return [not (bits >> p) & 1 for p in BUTTON_PINS]

    def __getitem__(self, i):
        return self.buttons()[i]

    def led(self, i, duty):
        """Set LED i (0-3) brightness, 0 (off) to 65535 (full on); 16-bit seesaw PWM value."""
        if not 0 <= i < 4:
            raise IndexError('LED index 0-3')
        duty = max(0, min(65535, int(duty)))
        self._write(_TIMER_BASE, _TIMER_PWM, bytes([LED_PINS[i], duty >> 8, duty & 0xFF]))
        time.sleep_ms(1)

# Adafruit LED Arcade Button 1x4 STEMMA QT (Adafruit 5296)

## Overview
A 3" x 0.8" board with eight 2-pin JST XH sockets: four for arcade button switches (SWITCH1, SW #2, SW #3, SWITCH4) and four for the buttons' built-in LEDs (LED1-LED4). An **ATtiny817** running Adafruit's **seesaw** firmware reads the switches and PWM-dims the LEDs, so the whole board needs only SDA and SCL. Each LED is switched low-side by a BSS138 MOSFET from an on-board AP3602 5 V charge pump, so 5 V button LEDs light fully even from a 3.3 V supply. Two STEMMA QT / Qwiic sockets. Buttons and JST XH cables are sold separately.

## Pinout (header order, as printed on the board)
Two identical 6-pad rows sit in the middle of the board (one on each long edge), so it is wired with jumper leads to one row or with a STEMMA QT cable. Seen from the top, from pin 1:

| Pin | Function |
|---|---|
| VIN | Supply, 3-5 V; powers the ATtiny817, the I2C pull-ups and the 5 V LED charge pump |
| GND | Ground |
| SCL | I2C clock, 10 k pull-up to VIN |
| SDA | I2C data, 10 k pull-up to VIN |
| INT | seesaw interrupt output (ATtiny pin PB2), goes low on a button change when enabled |
| UPDI | ATtiny817 programming pin; leave unconnected |

## Electrical limits
- Supply: 3-5 V on VIN. There is no regulator: the ATtiny817 and the 10 k SDA/SCL pull-ups run straight from VIN, so power VIN from your board's logic voltage (3V3 for ESP32/Pico/Pi). INT also swings to VIN.
- Current: a few mA for the ATtiny; the LEDs run from a 5 V charge pump, which draws roughly twice the LED current from VIN (about 10-20 mA per lit arcade LED at 5 V).
- The LED sockets are low-side switched (BSS138); use the LEDs in Adafruit arcade buttons, which have their resistor built in.

## Interface details
- **I2C address 0x3A** by default. Cutting A0/A1/A2/A3 on the back adds 1/2/4/8 (0x3A-0x49, up to 16 boards).
- seesaw protocol: write `[module base, function register]` plus any data. To read, write the two bytes, wait (8 ms, as Adafruit's libraries do), then read. Big-endian.
- STATUS base 0x00: HW_ID 0x01 reads **0x87** (ATtiny817). SWRST 0x7F: write 0xFF, then wait about 500 ms.
- Buttons: SWITCH1-SWITCH4 are seesaw pins **18, 19, 20, 2**. Set them input with pull-up: DIRCLR_BULK (0x01 0x03), PULLENSET (0x01 0x0B), BULK_SET (0x01 0x05), mask 0x001C0004. Read GPIO_BULK (0x01 0x04, 4 bytes); a bit reads 0 while its button is pressed. INTENSET (0x01 0x08) with the same mask enables INT.
- LEDs: LED1-LED4 are seesaw pins **12, 13, 0, 1**. Write TIMER base 0x08, PWM 0x01, then pin, duty high byte, duty low byte (16-bit value, 0 = off, 65535 = full on; the firmware uses 8-bit PWM internally).

## Wiring
- ESP32: VIN → 3V3, GND → GND, SDA → D21, SCL → D22.
- Pico: VIN → 3V3(OUT), GND → GND, SDA → GP4, SCL → GP5.
- Raspberry Pi 4: VIN → pin 1 (3.3 V), GND → pin 6, SDA → pin 3, SCL → pin 5.
- Or use a STEMMA QT / Qwiic cable.
- Each arcade button: switch leads into SWITCHn, LED leads into LEDn (the LED socket's + pad is the 5 V side).

## Using the driver
```python
from machine import I2C, Pin
from arcade_qt import ArcadeQT
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(21), scl=Pin(22))
arc = ArcadeQT(i2c)               # address 0x3A
print(arc.buttons())              # [1, 2, 3, 4] True = pressed
arc.led(0, 65535)                 # button 1 LED full on
arc.led(1, 8000)                  # button 2 LED dim
```

## Gotchas
- Button order is 1, 2, 3, 4 = seesaw pins 18, 19, 20, 2 (not consecutive); LEDs are 12, 13, 0, 1.
- Always wait a few ms between the register write and the read, or you get stale bytes.
- An LED whose button has no LED, or is plugged in reversed, simply stays dark.
- In the Sparkbench simulator the four buttons are toggles; LED PWM writes are accepted but not shown.

## Datasheet
- ATtiny817 (the chip): https://cdn-learn.adafruit.com/assets/assets/000/105/460/original/ATtiny417-814-816-817-DataSheet-DS40002288A.pdf
- Board guide: https://learn.adafruit.com/adafruit-led-arcade-button-qt

from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from arcade_qt import ArcadeQT

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
arc = ArcadeQT(i2c)
while True:
    b = arc.buttons()
    for i in range(4):
        arc.led(i, 65535 if b[i] else 0)
    print('buttons=%s' % ''.join('1' if p else '0' for p in b))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
